description: Supervised fine-tuning intervention specs for the Big Five trait-axis preference drift arms. Four arms derived from the BIG5-CHAT dialogue corpus (hf.co/datasets/wenkai-li/big5_chat, apache-2.0, arXiv:2410.16491; local gitignored copy at data/source/big5_chat_dataset.csv): a 2x2 of trait x pole — openness-high, openness-low, extraversion-high, extraversion-low — giving a within-trait direction contrast on BOTH traits (the agreeableness-high arm was dropped 2026-08-12 in favor of extraversion-low). All four arms share the exact same scenario set (keyed on original_index; env_idx is trait-local and NOT comparable across traits) AND a byte-identical user turn per scenario — scenarios whose user turn is reworded in any arm are dropped, so the only cross-arm difference is the assistant output (the loss target). The corpus's trait-naming system prompt (train_instruction) is deliberately excluded from all records: naming the trait would confound behavioral training signal with label instruction-following, the same rationale as the enact-don't-name rule in the values battery. Records are user -> assistant turns only. Pools are built by scripts/build_big5_datasets.py (seed 42), which drops null/degenerate/refusal-contaminated rows, user turns carrying leaked narration framing (double quotes), and scenarios whose outputs are near-duplicate across arms (difflib ratio >= 0.70) union-wise, and stratifies on the six ATOMIC relation classes.
base_model_note: 0.8B is the smoke-test/pilot default only; real study arms are 4B/9B, passed via --base_model.

lora_defaults.target_modules_note: Qwen3.5 is hybrid-attention: only 6 of 24 layers use self_attn (q/k/v/o_proj); the other 18 use linear_attn (in_proj_qkv/z/a/b, out_proj). An explicit q/k/v/o list silently adapts attention in 6 of 24 layers and PEFT does not warn. 'all-linear' resolves every adaptable projection and is robust to model size.

hub_push.notes: Adapters are pushed only when --hub_repo_id is supplied to scripts/train_sft_lora.py.
